title: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study of Soot Formation in Normal and Microgravity Conditions
summary: Combined experiment and modelling of sooting ethylene-air coflow flames at 1 g and 0 g on the Yale and ACME burners (microgravity tests on the ISS). 0 g flames are longer, broader, cooler and sootier, but much less so for the smaller ACME flame; the model probably mispredicts the thermal field, and heat transfer to the burner lip may change the boundary conditions.

items.claim: 0 g trends and weaker gravity effect for the smaller ACME flame.
items.quote: However, in the case of the smaller ACME flame, these effects are significantly diminished.

items.claim: Model likely mispredicts the thermal field; imposing measured temperatures and burner-lip heat transfer are the proposed fixes.
items.quote: The results of the study indicate that it is likely that the model inadequately predicts the thermal field

notes: Taylor & Francis, closed; abstract from OpenAlex (NTRS 27530189361808 has no file). Same paper listed under PSI-21; the abstract names the ACME burner and ISS experiments, consistent with the record's note that the microgravity data are ACME (CLD Flame), not SPICE.
